changes.what: R22 + HARNESS #7. The old single-log trim is replaced by section 4 'Log housekeeping', which has two parts. (a) Invoke-LogTrim: same rule as before (over 2 MB keeps the last 2000 lines), now applied to 10 paths: daily-backup.log, daily-backup.out, permission-gate/shadow.jsonl, ~/Library/Logs/everythingd.log, memory-compiler flush/compile/adjudicate.log, KeystoneOS outputs/morning/cadence.log, skill-router/skill_router.log and ~/.claude/skill_router.log. Missing files are skipped. All paths are built from $U/$LogDir/$DevRoot. It reads the tail into a variable, then rewrites the file. The old code piped Get-Content into Set-Content on the same file, which can truncate it before the read ends; that code never fired because the log stayed under 2 MB. The rewrite keeps the same inode, and lsof +fg confirmed that everythingd and the job's stdout append with O_APPEND, so live writers are safe. It honors -DryRun, and a failed trim is logged but not counted as an error. (b) Remove-OldFiles: deletes top-level files in KeystoneOS outputs/inventory and outputs/jobs older than 60 days, in place, never ~/.Trash. It only deletes files with YYYY-MM-DD in the name (every file there today is dated; no symlinks, hidden or undated files), logs one PRUNE line per folder and honors -DryRun. On the first real run it will trim shadow.jsonl (5.9 MB, 19,697 lines) and everythingd.log (5.6 MB) and delete about 92 inventory files and 90 jobs files. Both backup logs are under 2 MB today, so #7 is fixed by mechanism and no trim has fired on them yet.

HARNESS #3: the 2026-10-03 patch is ported into the current index step. 'INDEX full set' now logs '<n>/<m> paths exist, <k> .md files scanned' and the exit code, and adds '; no new content since last index' on 0. The .md count is deduped by FullName because the Inbox and Inbox/meetings roots overlap; that is about 4,300 files today, all local with no symlinks. With no input it records memsearch-index:no-input and logs 'NOT RUN - nothing to index' without running memsearch. Output not matching '^Indexed N chunks' records memsearch-index:unexpected-output.

HARNESS #4, in two halves. (1) Next run: new Get-IndexIncompleteRun runs before the start line. It reads the last DryRun=False block of daily-backup.log (tail 3000). If that block has 'INDEX path set' but no 'INDEX full set' or 'INDEX skipped', it records index-incomplete:<runId> and logs why. It only checks the immediately previous real run, so an old death is not raised forever. It is skipped while another backup pwsh is alive; the pgrep pattern '^[^ ]*pwsh .*daily-backup[.]ps1' excludes $PID and does not match caffeinate. The 2026-10-20 00:05 run had this same failure. (2) In-run: a catch on the index try logs 'INDEX full set: NO RESULT - <msg>' and records memsearch-index:no-result when the step throws. Testing showed that a throw escapes try/finally without this catch.

problems.problem: Low design note, no fix required. An index-incomplete:<prevRunId> error, which is about the previous run, makes the current run end ERROR. daily-backup-login.sh allows a second try when no run ended OK today and STARTS<2, so each detection costs one extra full backup that day (DB archive upload plus a 30-minute to 3-hour memsearch index). Separately, uv-prune stamps only on success, so on days when the cache is locked it is attempted up to twice (once per gated run), not strictly once. The implementer disclosed this.
problems.fix: None required; the brief asked for an error. If the extra run is unwanted, a later option is to write index-incomplete straight to .errors.log and leave it out of $Errors, so the current run's status reflects only its own work. Leave that to Eric.
